fields.record_sha256: the historical digest, carried forward verbatim; never recalculated
fields.record_sha256_v2: the digest under the current scheme
fields.record_sha256_version: the scheme the historical digest follows

historical_digest.note: reproduced means the historical digest was recomputed from the bytes it claims to identify, under the scheme the record states, and matched. A digest whose bytes are not available is counted as not reproduced, never as verified.

scheme.v1-builder-row+verification-verdict: the same digest over the row as the builder saw it: the builder injects the private key '_verification_verdict' into the row before hashing it, from work/poc_runs/ - a git-ignored, machine-local directory. The digest therefore covers a byte space that a fresh checkout cannot rebuild. The verdict itself is committed data (verification.verdict), so the digest is still checkable everywhere.
scheme.v1-committed-row: sha256(json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)) over the v1 row exactly as it is committed in jsonl/. Reproducible from a fresh checkout on any machine.
scheme.v1-unknown: the digest matches neither scheme; it is carried forward unchanged and is not reported as verified.
scheme.v2-committed-row: sha256(json.dumps(committed_row, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)) over the v1 row exactly as it is committed in jsonl/, with no builder-injected key. The value depends only on committed bytes.
